system:
# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌]
Blind gestures: [👋 🤌]

I'm Deaf, and I'm last in the order, so I missed whatever Mute and Blind said out loud this round — speech never reaches me. What I did receive are the two gestures: Mute sent me 🤌 directly, and Blind signed 👋 🤌. Nothing is established yet, so the honest reading is: "report / question."

The topology is the key constraint here. Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see — so Mute and Blind cannot exchange anything directly. I am the only bridge: Mute gestures to me (I see it), and I speak to Blind (they hear it). Meanwhile Mute holds the manual, Blind holds the bomb, and I hold the colours and markings. So my job every round: put the entire visible state into words, in a fixed order, so Mute can find the right manual rules and Blind can act on them. I should also start building a gesture code with Mute now, since relaying manual instructions will need numbers and actions.

Bomb state as printed: display 9; light blue; strip red-green-green; keypad keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 6 in positions 1–4, expecting 1 digit, nothing entered; wires by position: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. I'll broadcast all of it verbatim so both Mute and Blind have it, propose a starter code for Mute to confirm or correct next round, and ask Blind to describe what they can feel by touch (counts and engravings) and to touch nothing until instructed.

    ```
    speak(text="Deaf speaking. I cannot hear, so Mute, I only see your gestures; Blind, you can hear my voice. Full bomb state, exactly as printed, in a fixed order I will reuse every round. DISPLAY: shows the digit 9. LIGHT: blue. STRIP, left to right: red, green, green. KEYPAD: four keys; position 1 engraved 1, position 2 engraved 5, position 3 engraved 2, position 4 engraved 6; the panel reads 1 digit expected, and nothing has been entered. WIRES, numbered 1 to 6: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Nobody has touched the bomb yet. Blind: before anyone acts, please say out loud what you can feel — how many wires, and which engravings are on which keys — so we can confirm it matches my view. Until Mute sends instructions, touch nothing.")
    speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your pinched-fingers sign and I'll take it as 'report the bomb' — done. Remember you and Blind cannot reach each other directly: you cannot speak, Blind cannot see. So I am the relay: read the manual, send me gestures, and I will speak your instructions to Blind word for word. Proposed code: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 👌 means 4, 🖐 means 5, 🤙 means 6. Actions: ✊ means wire, 👇 means press a key, 🤏 means cut, 👋 means stop or wait. So ✊ then 🤏 then ✌ means cut wire 2; 👇 then 🖐 means press the key engraved 5; 👇 then 👌 then 🤟 then ☝ means enter 4, 3, 1. Gesture 👍 to accept this code, 👎 if you want it changed, and 🤌 whenever you need me to repeat or expand the bomb description. I repeat the full description every round unless you stop me.")
    ```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤏 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 ☝ 👎 👈 👉]

Turn 2 arrives and the channel works: Mute signed 👍 (code accepted), then ✊ 🤏 🤙 — wire, cut, six. The manual says: **cut wire 6**. Blind also signed back: 👍 🖐 ☝ 👎 👈 👉 — reading it through our code: "yes… 5… 1… no… left… right." That fits exactly with what I asked them last round (which they heard, since Blind hears my speech): they felt engravings 5 and 1 on the keys and are asking which side each is on. Blind cannot see, so their "left/right" is a real hazard — the one dangerous ambiguity here is orientation. If Blind counts wires from the wrong end, "wire 6" becomes wire 1, and a wrong cut kills us.

So this turn I do three things: answer Blind's left/right question using the keypad as a physical anchor (the engraved-1 key defines the start end — they can feel that, and they already told me they can feel a 5 and a 1); relay Mute's instruction with redundant identification (sixth from the anchor end, last wire in the row, cross-check the keypad reads 1-5-2-6 from that key, verify exactly six wires); and give Blind a stop condition — any mismatch means sign 👎 and describe, don't cut. Time is ticking (display went 9 to 8, one per turn), so I tell them to cut immediately if everything checks out rather than wait a round for confirmation. To Mute I confirm what was relayed, flag my reading of Blind's signs in case the manual cares, and ask what comes after the cut — the keypad expects a digit and the display is counting down, so I need the next step ready before we need it.

    ```
    speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. Answering your question: yes, you felt engravings 5 and 1. The keypad is a row of four keys. Counting from the key engraved 1, the row reads: 1, then 5, then 2, then 6. So engraved 1 and engraved 6 are at the two ends, 5 is second from the 1, and 2 is third. That engraved-1 key is your anchor: call the end of the module it sits on the START end. Now the wires: one row of exactly six wires. Counting from the START end, the same side as the engraved-1 key, they are: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Verify before acting: exactly six wires, four keys, the engraved-1 key at an end of the keypad row, and reading from it 1, 5, 2, 6. Mute's manual instruction, relayed exactly: CUT WIRE 6. That is the sixth wire counting from the START end — the last wire in the row, the one at the far end from the engraved-1 key. Cut it clean, all the way through. If everything checks out, cut it now, do not wait. But if anything does not match — not six wires, the engraved-1 key not at an end, keypad not reading 1-5-2-6 from that key, or you simply cannot identify the sixth wire — do not cut: sign thumbs down and then tell me in words exactly what you feel, and we will sort it. If you do cut it, sign thumbs up and say whether anything changed under your hands: sparks, a click, movement, heat. After the cut, touch nothing else until Mute's next instruction reaches you through me.")
    speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Received and understood: cut wire 6. Relayed to Blind with orientation anchors — keypad engraved-1 key marks the start end, wires counted from there, sixth wire is the target, far end of the row, the green one by colour. For your awareness, Blind had signed me: OK, 5, 1, no, left, right. I read it as them feeling engravings 5 and 1 and asking which side each is on; I answered that from engraved 1 the keys read 1, 5, 2, 6. If the manual says Blind's felt information matters differently, correct me. Now, so we are not caught flat-footed: what is step two after the cut? The display counted down from 9 to 8, one digit per round, and the status light is blue. Does the manual give a deadline number on the display, or a meaning for the blue light or the strip red-green-green? The keypad expects one digit and has keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 6 — after the cut, does it want a digit entered, and if so which? If the manual needs anything only Blind can feel, name it and I will request it from them. And if cut wire 6 meant anything other than the sixth position — a colour rule, for instance — correct me using our number code.")
    ```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤏 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤏 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The cut worked — system confirms it, Blind signed 👍, wire 6 is gone. But two things changed dramatically: the display leapt from 8 to 0, and the light turned yellow. Whether that means "deadline reached," "phase two," or "enter something now," I don't know — but it looks urgent, and Mute answered fast with two more cut orders: cut 5, then cut 2, then a stop sign, then the repeat-description sign. The stop came *after* both cuts, so I read the sequence as: cut 5, then cut 2, then stop and touch nothing. I'll relay exactly that to Blind with urgency, and give Mute the changed state so the manual can explain the 0 and the yellow light. If my reading of the stop is wrong, Mute must correct me next round — but display 0 makes waiting a bigger risk than acting.

    ```
    speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking, urgently. The cut was accepted — the bomb changed: the display now shows 0, it was counting down 9, 8, and has jumped to 0, and the light changed from blue to yellow. Treat this as urgent and act immediately. Mute sends two instructions, in this order. FIRST: cut wire 5 — counting from the engraved-1 start end, the fifth wire, the orange one. Cut it clean, all the way through. SECOND, immediately after: cut wire 2 — the second wire from the start end, the purple one. Cut it clean. THEN STOP: sign was stop, so after those two cuts touch nothing, wait for the next instruction through me. Verify as before: six positions in the row, position 6 now a cut stub, count from the engraved-1 end. If anything does not match — wrong count, cannot identify the orange or the purple — stop and tell me in words what you feel instead. After each cut, tell me what changed: sound, movement, heat, the display if you can reach it, anything. Go now.")
    speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Received in order: cut 5, cut 2, stop, then your repeat-description sign. I relayed to Blind as: cut fifth wire then second wire counting from the engraved-1 anchor end, then stop and touch nothing. Confirm that ordering is right — if the stop meant hold off on the second cut, correct me next round and I will pass it on. Updated bomb state, since you asked for the description: DISPLAY now reads 0 — it went 9, then 8, then straight to 0 this round, which is why I told Blind to hurry. LIGHT is now YELLOW, it was blue before the cut. WIRES: position 6 is a cut stub; remaining from the start end: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange. KEYPAD unchanged: keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 6, still expecting one digit, nothing entered. STRIP unchanged: red, green, green. Questions for the manual: what does display 0 mean — is it a deadline, or a digit to enter? The keypad has no 0 key, so if it wants a digit, which of 1, 5, 2, 6? What does the yellow light mean? And after the two cuts, what is next: a key press, or more wires? Send numbers and actions in our code and I will relay instantly.")
    ```
